newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle not well tested - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle not well tested - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids were firm at $68.00 per cwt, steady with last week's active trade, but there were not enough sales at that level to fully test the market, feedlot sources said.

About 100 heifers sold at $68.00 in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and would likely grade select and choice, the sources said. There were no trades reported in Kansas, except for a handful of holstein steers, they said.
Most owners held firm to asking levels of $69.00 to $70.00 amid outlooks for continued strength in beef prices, the feedlot sources said.

Beef prices Monday were quoted up $0.57 to $1.15 per cwt, with 174 fabricated beef loads sold. Heavyweight choice beef was quoted up $1.15 at $107.38, up $2.25 from a week ago and at its highest level since March 5, USDA statistics showed.
Beef was supported by strong demand from retailers booking for beef features this month, particularly for the Memorial Day holiday weekend, market sources said.

Memorial Day, May 26, is traditionally the largest beef consumption day of the year, followed closed by Labor Day, September 1 and Independence Day, July 4, according to the National Cattlemen's Beef Association.
